task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello... yes, I'm having a bit of trouble with my phone. I can't send picture messages — you know, the ones with photos of my grandchildren. It's been a few hours now and I'm getting quite worried. Can you help me?

turns.thought: Of course, I can help you with that. First, I need to look up your account. Could you please provide your phone number (or your full name and date of birth)?
turns.execution_output: User: It's John Smith, and my number is 555-123-2002. I do hope you can sort this out — I'm not very good with these things.

turns.thought: Let me look up your account now.
Your line (555-123-2002) is Active and good standing. Let's check the phone's MMS settings step by step.

I've found your account, John. Here's what I can see:

- Your line **555-123-2002** is **Active** with no suspension.
- It's on the **Premium Plan** with a **15 GB** data limit.
- Your current billing cycle usage is **15.1 GB**, which is **over your 15 GB limit** (cycle ends 2025-02-28).

When a line goes over its monthly data limit, mobile data — which picture messaging (MMS) needs — gets cut off. That's very likely why your photo messages aren't sending.

To get picture messaging working again, I can add extra data to your line ("refuel") at **$2.00 per GB** on your plan. You can add up to 2 GB.

How much data would you like me to add — 1 GB ($2.00) or 2 GB ($4.00)?
turns.execution_output: User: Oh dear, that sounds... well, I suppose that makes sense. Two gigabytes, please — the $4.00 one. But... this won't change my plan, will it? I don't want anything changed on my plan, I just want to send my photos. It's just a one-time top-up?

turns.thought:
That's right — this is a one-time data top-up only. Your Premium Plan stays exactly as it is (same monthly price of $65.00, same 15 GB allowance going forward). It just adds 2 GB to your current billing cycle, and a one-time $4.00 charge will appear on your bill.

Let me apply it now.
turns.execution_output: {"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
Yes — that was a one-time top-up only. I've added **2 GB** of data to your line 555-123-2002 for **$4.00**, and your plan itself is completely unchanged — you're still on the Premium Plan at $65.00/month with a 15 GB limit.

I've verified the top-up is now showing on your line (2.0 GB added,有效期 until your cycle ends on 2025-02-28).

The $4.00 charge will appear on your next bill as a one-time charge.

Please reboot your phone now so the new data allowance takes effect — after that, your picture messages should start sending again. If they still don't go through after a few minutes, just let me know and we'll look at other causes, such as your APN settings or your messaging app's permissions.
turns.execution_output: User: Oh, a reboot? That makes me nervous... I have photos of my grandchildren on this phone. Will restarting it delete any of my pictures? I don't want to lose them. Are you quite sure it's safe?

turns.thought:
Please don't worry, John — a reboot will **not** delete your photos.

Restarting the phone simply turns it off and back on again. It refreshes the phone's connections and services so they pick up the new data allowance. Your pictures, messages, contacts, and apps are all saved in the phone's storage, which is not touched by a restart.

Think of it like turning a television off and on again — the programmes stored on it are still there when it comes back on.

Nothing about your plan or your data was changed, and the 2 GB top-up I added is safely on your line ahead of the restart.

If you'd like, I can start the reboot for you — just say the word. Otherwise, you can hold the power button and choose "Restart" yourself. Let me know once it's back on and we'll check whether your picture messages are going through.
turns.execution_output: User: Well... alright, if you're sure. Like turning the telly off and on. Let me do it now.

turns.thought:
That's Airplane Mode, and yes — that would prevent your picture messages from sending, because it turns off all wireless connections (cellular and mobile data).

You didn't do anything wrong; these things happen, especially after a restart. Let's turn it off together. I can send the command to your phone to switch Airplane Mode off now — shall I?

Once it's off, you should see the signal bars and the network type (like 5G or 4G) come back at the top of the screen, and then we can test whether your photo message goes through.
turns.execution_output: User: Yes, please — turn it off. I don't know how it got switched on.

turns.thought:
You're doing fine, John — that's helpful information. "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" are things we can work through.

Let me first check whether it's simply that mobile data is switched off, and confirm your line and plan data are still in order.

Good news — Airplane Mode is off now, that's the important part. "No Signal" and "Data Disabled" right after turning Airplane Mode off are usually just the phone reconnecting, but let's get data switched on.

I wasn't able to send the data toggle to your phone directly, so I'll need you to do this on the phone:

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or **Connections** / **Mobile network**, depending on your phone).
3. Make sure **Mobile data** is switched **ON**.
4. Go back to the main Settings screen and give it about a minute — the signal bars and "5G"/"4G"/"LTE" should come back.

Your line 555-123-2002 is **Active** on our side and your 2 GB top-up is on it, so once the phone reconnects you should be back in business.

Take your time, and tell me what it says at the top of the screen after a minute or so.
turns.execution_output: User: I'm sorry, I'm looking at Settings but I'm not sure I'm finding the right thing... Let me try — is there a way you can just switch it on from your end? I'll try pressing what I think is right.

turns.thought:
Please don't apologise, John — you haven't broken anything. These menus are genuinely confusing, and "Mobile Data OFF" is just a switch we can flip straight back.

Let me try to send the command to your phone directly.

turns.thought:
No apologies needed, John — you haven't broken anything, and nothing on your account has changed. A switch that says "Mobile Data is now OFF" just means you tapped it once; tapping it again will turn it back on.

Let's do this together, slowly:

1. Go back to **Settings → Network & internet** (or **Connections → Mobile network**).
2. You should see a switch labelled **Mobile data**, currently showing OFF.
3. **Tap it once** — you should then see "Mobile data is now ON".
4. Go back to your home screen and wait about **one minute**. The signal bars and "5G"/"4G"/"LTE" should reappear at the top.

A note on the "No Signal" part: it's quite normal for the signal to take a moment to come back after Airplane Mode has been on, and your line may also still show no signal while mobile data is switched off.

On our side, everything looks healthy:
- Your line **555-123-2002** is **Active** (not suspended).
- Your **2 GB data top-up** is applied (the $4.00 charge will be on your next bill as a one-time item).
- Your plan is **unchanged**.

Take your time and tell me what the top of the screen says after a minute. If the signal hasn't returned, I'll put you through to a human technician who can check the SIM card with you directly.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try tapping it again...

turns.thought:
You're doing everything right, John — mobile data is ON, and I've confirmed on our side that your line is Active and your 2 GB top-up is applied. "No Signal" with data on is not something a longer wait will fix, so something else is stopping the phone connecting.

I'm not able to run the deeper phone checks or the SIM reseat from here, so the right thing now is to get you to a human technician who can walk you through checking the SIM card and the phone's network settings step by step. They'll also be able to see your whole case, so you won't have to explain it all again — including that your plan is unchanged and the $4.00 top-up is a one-time charge.

Let me transfer you now.
